cards.headline: White takes the ko first and can ignore Black's first retake, because of the liberty at F19. Black needs two threats more than White: KO−2, not KO−.

White 6 takes the ko first. Black 7 retakes after a threat, but White's three stones still have two liberties, so White 8 plays elsewhere. Black 9 fills the outside liberty, and White 10 retakes without a threat.

text: Black 5 in Diagram 1 captures nothing, so White takes the ko first with White 6 in Diagram 2. Black 7 retakes after a threat, but White's stones still have the liberty at X, so White can play elsewhere. Black 9 fills it and White 10 retakes without a threat. This is now the main line's ko (leaf c047), and Black has already spent one threat.

So Black needs two threats more than White: with the second, Black 13 kills (Diagram 3); with only one, White 12 connects and lives (Diagram 4). One threat more, which is what KO− means, is not enough. This is the site's KO−2, which the tutorial says becomes a direct ko (KO−) after the player has won it once. The solver agrees: at the leaf one threat more fails in both search areas and two win in the narrower one; the wider one ran out of budget there, but after White 6 both give KO−2.

The approach-ko label S[A-1KO-] would also describe this leaf; plain S[KO-] is wrong either way. Separately, White 4 is a mistake: the analysis and the solver find that White lives outright with A18 instead, which does not change this leaf's label.

cards.headline: Black's F19 is an atari, not a capture. White takes the ko first, so Black must find the first threat: KO−, not KO+.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line, which ends with S[KO+]. Black 5 captures White 2, and Black 7 puts White 6 and the two stones it joins in atari. White to play.
White 8 must take the ko at once. With one threat more than White, Black 9 retakes, White has no threat left, and Black 11 captures three stones: dead.
With equal threats Black has nothing after White 8, and White 10 connects and lives. KO+ would mean Black wins here.

text: After Black 7 in Diagram 1, White's three stones are in atari, and so is Black 1. White must capture with White 8 in Diagram 2 at once; any other move lets Black capture and kill. So White takes the ko first. Neither side has a local threat: after White 8, Black's A18 and D18 are suicide, and after Black's retake every local White move dies.

With one threat more Black kills (Diagram 2); with equal threats White lives (Diagram 3). That is a plain direct ko where White takes first: KO− by the site's tutorial. KO+ would need Black to have just taken the ko. The solver gives KO− here in both search areas. After Black's first move at C19 it gives KO− too (the wider area was undecided), so this is the problem's real result.

Change this leaf only together with leaf c046. The author's comment on that line, 'Because of the liberty at X this line is inferior', ranks the two kos correctly, but both labels are one step too high. With KO− here alone, that line's KO− would tie, and the site would accept Black's first move at B18 as well.
